item.title: "Hikaru is definitely not the best online Blitz player in the world. Magnus is still just far away best" — Olexandr Bortnyk
item.description: Olexandr Bortnyk shared his opinion on Hikaru Nakamura in an interview with Chess with Mustreader. Bortnyk believes that Nakamura is not the best online Blitz player. Olexandr notes that Magnus is the best by a large margin.
item.content:encoded:
Olexandr Bortnyk shared his opinion on Hikaru Nakamura in an interview with Chess with Mustreader. Bortnyk believes that Nakamura is not the best online Blitz player. Olexandr notes that Magnus is the best by a large margin.

“Everyone thinks Hikaru is the best online Blitz player in the world. I would say that I disagree with that.

He is in the top, but he is definitely not the best. Magnus is still just far away best. Hikaru is still in the top, but I don’t think he is top-1. Maybe not even top-3. Top-2, let’s say…

Obviously, Magnus is number one still. Someone would say: “Magnus is different already. It’s not the same Magnus as he was.” Good luck with that.”

Olexandr Bortnyk — Ukrainian GM

Hikaru Nakamura holds first place on the Chess.com Blitz leaderboard. The gap between Nakamura and the second-highest rated player, Magnus Carlsen, is 75 points. Hikaru reached the record Blitz rating on Chess.com of 3500 points in early October.

Credit: Yoav Nisenbaum / FIDE

item.title: Hans Niemann Wins Freestyle Friday with 9 Points on October 23
item.description: Hans Moke Niemann scored 8 victories and 2 draws to win the October 23 Freestyle Friday tournament with 9/11 points. Runner-up Sina Movahed won 8 times, drew 2 times, and lost once, which led him to finish second with 9 points.
item.content:encoded:
Hans Moke Niemann scored 8 victories and 2 draws to win the October 23 Freestyle Friday tournament with 9/11 points. Runner-up Sina Movahed won 8 times, drew 2 times, and lost once, which led him to finish second with 9 points.

Freestyle Friday is a weekly Chess.com event for verified titled players, featuring the Chess960 variant. The event is an 11-round Swiss tournament with a 3+1 time control featuring a $1,000 weekly prize fund. This event is a part of the 2026 Freestyle Friday Championship, the winner of which will qualify for the 2027 FIDE Freestyle Chess World Championship.

Credit: FIDE

item.title: Lichess Ends Its Boycott of US Chess
item.description: Lichess announced the resumption of cooperation with US Chess. The chess platform explains that they are satisfied with the changes made in the federation. Lichess notes that US Chess made changes to maintain a safe and supportive environment within the organization.
item.content:encoded:
Lichess announced the resumption of cooperation with US Chess. The chess platform explains that they are satisfied with the changes made in the federation. Lichess notes that US Chess made changes to maintain a safe and supportive environment within the organization.

Lichess named several changes in the US Chess structure. US Chess leadership involved in the mishandling of historical allegations are no longer in such positions. Recent leadership changes have led to more open communication. US Chess introduced organization-wide changes in policy.

Lichess states that these changes have given them confidence that future incidents will be dealt with appropriately. Lichess is lifting its boycott and will resume official broadcasts of US Chess events. Lichess will resume providing additional support to chess organizations.

Lichess announced its boycott of both the US Chess Federation and the Saint Louis Chess Club in 2023. The reason was concerns about their accountability for mishandling sexual misconduct allegations.

Lichess resumed cooperation with the Saint Louis Chess Club in 2025. US Chess resolved its dispute with WGM Jennifer Shahade in March 2026. Shahade publicly accused GM Alejandro Ramirez of sexual misconduct in 2023.

Credit: PokerStars
